title: Stops trancribing, yet still utilizing resources
body:
Using large-v3 model with basic settings (everything default), the program somewhat stuck/freezes/stops at a certain point (few minutes into a 90 minutes long audio), yet the GPU usage still at 80-90%, the fans are still spinning, there is activity in the background, yet the progress has been halted for some reason. 

How can I debug/test out/create logs during it to determine what's wrong it?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: You could experiment with a different model, such as large-v2, to see if the issue continues. If the issue doesn't recur, it's likely that the program is getting stuck in the decoding process, possibly entering a loop because of temperature fallback.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> The GPU temperature stayed in the mid 60s degrees during that 15 mins while I let it run.

I'm referring to the temperature fallback in the sampling process, not the actual temperature of your GPU. LOL

See https://arxiv.org/pdf/1612.02695.pdf

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Yeah I deleted that comment, sorry! (newbie here)

So what value should I set to that setting to avoid happening this again? (I also switch to v2 to see how that handles it)

Will read that pdf, thank you.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Is there any way to manually increase the GPU usage? It sits in the 30% range,  but would be nice if it can utility full capacity as well.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> So what value should I set to that setting to avoid happening this again?

You can lower the `--entropy-thold`, which will enhance the likelihood of hallucinations but simultaneously decrease the risk of getting trapped in a loop.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> Is there any way to manually increase the GPU usage?

NO. However, you can transcribe multiple files at the same time.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> are there definitive parameter values that would always booster the output (experience) without sacrificing other aspects?

AFAIK, there aren't any parameters like that. If there were specific parameter values that consistently enhanced output quality, like you mentioned, we would have already set them as defaults. Take the beam size, for instance, it's preset to 5.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> Just asking, because I've read somewhere that "beam size", "best of being" and "patience" settings being set to higher/lower values can lead to various end results. All part of being a AI program I guess.
 
Absolutely. Additionally, there are various sampling strategies to explore, such as `top P` and `top K`. I'm sure you'll find the learning journey through the AI world to be quite fascinating.
